partners.mechanism_chain: F12 (HGNC:3530) —DISRUPTS→ Kinin-Kallikrein System (REACT:R-HSA-116908); Kinin-Kallikrein System (REACT:R-HSA-116908) —INCREASES→ Bradykinin (CHEBI:20720); Bradykinin (CHEBI:20720) —LEADS_TO→ Hereditary Angioedema Type 3 (MONDO:0012526); F12 (HGNC:3530) —DISRUPTS→ Congenital Factor XII Deficiency (MONDO:0009315); Kinin-Kallikrein System (REACT:R-HSA-116908) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital Factor XII Deficiency (MONDO:0009315). Mutations in F12 lead to dysfunction of Factor XII. In HAE type 3, haploinsufficiency of F12 results in dysregulation of the kinin-kallikrein system, leading to excessive bradykinin production and angioedema. In congenital Factor XII deficiency, loss-of-function mutations in F12 directly impair its role in the coagulation cascade and can also affect the kinin-kallikrein system, manifesting as a bleeding disorder and potentially contributing to angioedema-like symptoms due to bradykinin dysregulation.

Mutations in F12 cause hereditary angioedema type 3 by disrupting the contact activation pathway, leading to angioedema. C1QBP, a mitochondrial protein, plays a role in mitochondrial respiratory chain complex assembly and also interacts with components of the contact activation pathway. **How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in SERPING1 in patients with hereditary angioedema type 3 that do not impair C1 inhibitor function or its regulatory roles in the complement and bradykinin pathways would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis in the dysregulation of the complement and bradykinin cascades provides a common therapeutic target for both conditions, potentially allowing for the development of drugs that modulate these pathways to treat angioedema and related symptoms across both disease types.
